Brief Updated Review:

Player numbers are dwindling but, you will still find a game. Combat is still fun and rewarding. Class creation system is great and keeps me invested. No Micro-transactions. You will get curb stomped by some players who probably have not put the game down since release. I play purely for the chaos of frontline and invasion (Both objective games). 40 vs 40 games when the servers are somewhat full. If you have a poor internet connection, then you probably want to avoid this game as a spike in your ping can be fatal. This game will drop new players and old players together, but it is probably for the best (See full updated review for my reasoning). Finally, players have had a few server stability issues.

Overall, still fun if you do not care about your kill/death ratio. Come for the chaos and class creation system. You will get better and not fall for feints eventually, took me a lot of time. I really hope this game gets a spike in popularity as it is a great game. 


Full updated review:

I reviewed this back in 2019 and some of my points still stand, but I thought I should update it since a fair bit has changed. I was level 22 when I first wrote the review and as of when I add this, I am sitting at level 80.

To start off this game is still great, I have been coming back to Mordhau through out the years and have seen the best of what the game has to offer and the worst of it. It is a difficult game to get back into as you will get that high level player that will wipe out the server. I am level 80 with 300+ hours but you can find players who are at level 200 and it is a slow levelling process. 

New players and old players:

You may think it is bad for an experienced player and a new player to be thrown together and well… it is but the active player numbers are not exactly high. 

How Chivalry (the game that Mordhau is based off) handle new players was it gave those level 1 – 15 their own server to learn. This was great but high-level players would just create a smurf accounts so they could join those games. Also, when you hit level 16 you were dropped with everyone else and at that point players had far more advanced techniques. Level 1 – 15 on Chivalry was a chaotic mess of luck. Whereas 16+ was a lot of feinting, avatar abuse, ect.
So, it is probably for the best that new players and old players are put together. As they will learn a lot faster. 
(I welcome feedback on this topic as it is what discourages new players from enjoying themselves on Mordhau)

Closing thoughts:

Appreciate all feedback I have been giving never expected a review to do this well. I want Mordhau to stand the test of time as it is fun and great to comeback to.  Probably gave the impression that the game is dying. I would love to be wrong, but I am finding myself using the server browser to find fuller games instead of pressing quickplay. I took a break around patch 18 – 19 and came back January of 2021 so it feels like a lot has happened in Mordhau in these past 3 months.

2019
For existing players:

Yes, it is rage inducing. Yes, that sword did hit you. "How?" very easily, you didn't block it. Player with maul wondering how they lost to a player with a training sword? All weapons are different. Each with their own speeds. Yes, some weapons hit harder than others. Some are longer than others and yes that guy on your team blind firing the catapult DOES deserve to die, no one will blame you if that player was to disappear. 

You must accept that 80% of the time, you are the one who messed up. There is that 20% due to internet connectivity and sometimes lack of hit registration (Seen players complain but never happened to me). 

If you ever struggle when playing, try out third person. You might find yourself surviving 3 vs 1 encounters. Also, try to create custom classes and look at the weapon stats. Also, there is an offline mode you can use to practise against AI.

For potential buyers:

If you anger easily or prone to rage quit, then this game isn't for you.

It is rage inducing and you will question half the hits you take/inflict. But in a 32 vs 32 match it is very chaotic. Allies and enemies charging into one another and then immediately stopping because they really want to protect their Kill Death ratio. That lute player somehow playing Metallica... There is a lot to take in. A load of unique classes as well as a class creation system. You want to have 3 lutes on your person at all time? Go for it. 

Gameplay: 

The weapon combat is great using your mouse and avatar to make swings hit faster or slower. The various strengths of each weapons. For example, spears are better at stabbing than for swinging. Weapons will collide with surfaces which will stop their momentum. Parry’s and feints are available allowing you to psyche out your opponent. Armour affects your movement and overall damage you can take. Armour is located on three areas: Head, Torso and Legs. There is chambering which I do not fully understand and most of the time I’m to mystified by it to realise I should strike back.
You can create your own class which is a ton of fun. The system works by having a limited amount of points and every item costing points dependant on strength of item. There is medical equipment you can carry that helps survivability of you or your team. There’s an engineer class that lets you build fortification (Only in specific areas) and ballistae. Engineer tools are available for create your own class. You also have access to perks when creating classes. Bows I do not personally use. Prefer to swing a sword in a hazardous environment than shoot from a safe distance.  There’s probably a lot of information I’ve missed, feel free to fact check me.

Extra (Just things):


There are 3 stages you will go through when fighting larger skirmishes with your allies in MORDHAU.

Stage 1: "I'll just use stabs and therefore, won't hurt my allies!"

Stage 2: "Whoops sorry! Didn't mean to hit you there!"

Stage 3: "Why are you standing within axe-swinging distance?!?! Do you have a death wish?!?"

If you see a lute player on the opposite team. Let them pass, they’re likely late for their gathering and deserve the right of way.

Now the player base is divided personality wise. You have the tryhards which every game must be a win otherwise the game is shit. The casual players who will emote and are more likely to be friendly. You will have the new players who can often be found wondering to parts unknown and endangering the wild life (Other players with their dam catapults). You also get the team killing for horses or siege equipment. I like horse as much as anyone, but I’ll dismount for class with a longer weapon than mine and of course if they… ASK! Yea, no one ask for anything and just expects you to know better? Players complain when they’re killed by anything. I had a guy complain after I killed him with his own throwing axe. Not all players are like this, but you only notice the annoying ones who team kill, disrupt funny moments, etc…

The community… Most are ok… But holy crap do players get mad. Either I didn’t notice it before or Crossroads has unleashed MORDHAU players inner demons. I’m no angel, I get mad too. Holy crap though, Toxic as all hell some days. However, there are a few funny players that make it worthwhile. On Grad me and an opponent took turns firing the ballista, it was surprisingly civil. I would fire, step away then he would fire and ect.

Also, lute players are still alive and well. I’m disappointed in the backstabbing ones though… 

Feel free to correct me on any points.

So. Imagine this. You were playing a medieval game called Chivalry Medieval Warfare. The community became elitist and conceited. The combat system consisted of only a few mechanics - more notably - the dizzying spastic 360 swings of a violent, bloodthirsty Knight who had too much to drink. The level design was fine, but the graphics were subpar. Overall, it felt like something was missing. Like the developers half-assed their game and didn't put much thought into it.

Well, guess what?

You have Mordhau now. A game which not only refines the fundamentals of Chivalry Medieval Warfare, but introduces other mechanics of its own. It also cuts out all the bad bits about Chivalry such as the effectiveness of 360ing like a total moron and hoping you hit something, with varying chances for success. 

Imagine immersing yourself into a graphically beautiful world with fantastic textures and a high degree of customization. Imagine being able to customize your character down to the individual pieces of equipment, as well as modifying your armour's tint and the various potential patterns an item might have with numerous colours from a palette. You can sculpt your character's face, customise various voice presets to fit your desires, or become a gnome, like someone I saw in the game. And it was very on point to how one looks like. Now, allow me to shift your attention over to the weapons. You can customise not only the hilt and the guard, but also how the blade looks, and are permitted to colourise various parts of the weapon. 

If Chivalry - despite it's shortcomings - did not enthrall you enough as you might have wanted it to, you now have a game which adds many more mechanics to enrich the gameplay of the game. You can now morph - that is, you can initiate a stab or a slash and transition into the other attack. You can now block arrows in mid-air like Aragorn. The attack combinations flow into each other and are seamless. Even something like a slash can be influenced to come from below or from the sides depending on your mouse orientation. 

So, why not buy the game that forfills all the needs that Chivalry neglected and treats you like a real man? No microtransactions, you earn the gold in game. Go on. Do what you want to do. Buy the game, and decapitate some heads, whilst screaming in a high-pitched farmer boy's voice.

Six years ago, I probably would've wrote a glowing review for this game. But after those six long years of playing this game, I fully realize now that this game was in its prime when no-one knew what they were doing. We still remembered how to not take this game seriously in the slightest and just have fun. The writing was on the wall when veteran players started offering "coaching" in exchange for real money. In my eyes, the playerbase completely lost the plot for why most of us got into this game in the first place after that.

In the game's current state, I cannot with any honesty or integrity recommend this game to a fresh player. Do I still enjoy playing this game and have some of the best memories of my life in it? Absolutely, but you are not me. You don't have 2.5k hours of blood, toil, tears, and sweat under your belt. If you jump into this game now, you are going to get your teeth kicked in A LOT. Trying to learn and get better while going up against the players that still stick around in this game is going to be a very hard lesson in how you can do everything right and still lose, and that's not your fault, that's just the reality this game finds itself in now.

I still consider this the superior game compared to Chivalry II, but one aspect that I must concede that Chivalry II does better than Mordhau is "Dumb Fun". Ways to provide yourself with brevity and comedic relief to alleviate the feeling of having someone's digital boot constantly stomping on your face. This key aspect I feel has been slowly withering away as time goes on in the life of this game.

Do yourself a favor, spend the 30$ on something you know you'll enjoy from the start like a meal from your favorite restaurant or a trip to the movies with your partner. Anything really that you can enjoy simply for what it is, and not for what it can potentially be.

it was fun, but now the only people playing it are super veterans that so vastly outskill you, that you have no time to learn. and most of them are insanely toxic. the sparring servers are decent. it just feel super dead, wish it wasn't the case because it was super fun back at release

Unfortunately, Mordhau is in a rough spot today. The player base is small, and the only players left are absolute sweat lords who have mastered every mechanic, making it pretty brutal for new players.

That being said, when this game was at its peak, it was truly something special. For such a small development team, they created a masterpiece. The massive team battles were absolute chaos, and there was nothing else quite like fighting alongside your brethren in the middle of a full scale medieval battle. Some of my fondest gaming memories came from those moments, fighting side by side with your squad, holding your ground as enemies slowly surrounded you. The combat was satisfying, the battles felt alive, and even things like catapults and archers had their place without ruining the melee focused experience.

Mordhau had so much potential, and it’s sad to see where it ended up. I wouldn’t recommend it to a brand new player today, but I’ll always cherish the years when this game was at its peak.

I want to start off this review by saying I absolutely loved this game and have so many good memories and experiences with the modding and regular community. I used to consistently be in the top 200 of duelist and started playing back when the player base was in the 60,000 range. I only mention that because I want the reader to know I have a good idea of this game, what it USED to be, and what it is NOW.

Mordhau's community used to be extremely full of life and humor, very dark humor, lol. Sadly, nowadays it's become a shell of its former self and is hollow. What used to be creative back-and-forths that consisted of ducking or jumping over a person's blade, being disarmed, and having to fight only with your hands, and fighting 1v5, has turned into what most of the duels were like when I was playing in the top 200. It took a long time, but the general player base finally understood how to push the combat system until it cracked, and the devs helped. This is horrible because it gives any new player almost no chance to grow and learn how to play the game.

Once I started playing in the top 200, I hated the game I used to love so much. Broken animations to make parrying a hit impossible started to become a trademark in every opponent I faced. Most of the higher-level players, probably past the top 1000, knew which weapons you could abuse the animations with to get cheap hits, and about half of them would abuse it. I thought once I broke past that layer, I'd be fighting the people who were just more mechanically sound at the game and continue to have creative duels. It broke my heart to realize the number of people abusing the animations just kept getting higher the more I climbed until it was only that. I remember stopping mid-duel and having a conversation with the person I was fighting about it. I'll never forget him completely agreeing with me and saying, "It's the only way to keep climbing at this point. I hate it, but there's nothing else to do." I was left no choice but to stop dueling because I was surpassing the people who dueled to have a competitive 1v1 and stuck against the people who just wanted to win.

This is what base Mordhau has become. Almost all of the player base has soured into hateful people who just want to "win." I've almost only covered how the combat has turned toxic, but it goes hand in hand with the attitude of those people as well.

Base Mordhau used to be about ♥♥♥♥♥ and giggles, even for players like me who were trying to 1v5 when our entire objective was being taken, lmao. If you were stomping someone in a duel, about half the players (below top 1000) would stop and start to tell you why you were losing and show you how to improve. Bards would download mods so you could hear your favorite movie soundtrack being played on a lute. You'd have high-level players running around using only fists wearing no armor, fighting the new guys who would be shocked they couldn't land one hit on someone with no weapon. The voice actors just screaming half the time. It was such a beautiful and refreshing game.

I want to say I miss this game, but knowing what it's become, I can't. I just miss the way it made me feel.

The game is amazing in and of itself. The combat is glorious and the most fulfilling from any game I've ever played. It's rock paper scissors mixed with two for flinching, on the surface. The interplay of the various elements and mechanics is glorious, and feels good to master.

But you probably won't master them. I've been playing this game since release effectively and I can tell you this

Levels 0-100 are generally considered the learning curve to just get used to the basics. The Tutorial is hot garbage that doesn't teach you any of the true essentials, assuming a new player even plays it. There's very little reason to do so beyond the gold bonus you get for doing so.

If you want to learn the basics you need someone to teach you. Swing manipulation. Accels, drags, chambers, even ripostes some players don't understand.

Dueling and team fighting require entirely different skillsets. Being good at one won't make you good at the other.

The Devs dont know how to balance team skill either. Ought to take the average level of every player on the server, and then try to make two teams with approximate combination of skill. Not that it will save you.

Players have complained about "team stacking for ages" it's a myth. At the time of writing team selection has been disabled. Teams get crushed more thoroughly now than they ever have before. Showing us that the issue wasn't that good players would join the same team previously to win games. That simply using autoselect at start without any true means of balancing would lead to this situation. Now as a level 218 player I can't even swap to the losing team to try and balance things myself.

The Devs don't play their own game. The Devs don't moderate their own community. they don't push content at anything close to a reasonable speed, and if something's broken expect at least 6 months of sitting on the busted issue without seeing a resolution, or a partial fix at that.

They change things drastically from patch to patch, nerf non issues because they themselves struggle with a mechanic or weapon, and don't listen to feedback from the community. They make the same mistakes over and over, and don't really learn from it. 

I love this game, but it's garbage on so many levels for new players.

If you can handle the bullshit it's a diamond. Rough. Uncut. Brilliant under all the bullshit. But the devs should sell the IP to someone else who actually gives a shit.

It's the best in the genre, and one of my favorite games, so it's painful not to recommend this.
However, it is the honest thing to do. My reasoning is below:

Unfortunately the player count plateaued a long time ago and only seems to get smaller month over month. We've finally dropped below the 1,000 player count peak on PC, and console players maybe add a few hundred on top of that. Only those with an undying love for game are still playing, which means if you're new, you're going to have a hard time understanding why you're getting absolutely destroyed by anyone you run into purely due to mechanical depth that is not immediately apparent, and poorly taught via in-game sources.

Triterion have more or less abandoned the game, with the last update being nearly a year ago, and that was a PvE horde mode about demons in a game people obviously picked up for PvP. It was odd to watch them have a potential strangle-hold on a genre only to lop off its' head and leave it festering in a dumpster with the occasional spritzing of Febreze to keep the smell at bay. Also, to be clear, Chivalry 2 was never a threat to that.

I believe they also started work on an unannounced new IP some time ago, so it's unlikely they'll return to drop new [PvP] maps, weapons, or a balancing update barring a 10th anniversary. I'm not going to include the questionable cosmetics they've released in an attempt to further fund whatever they're up to now. I hope it's good, but after witnessing the development cycle of this game, I wouldn't go out of my way to pre-order it.

It's only fair you know what you're getting into if you are going to pick this up on sale for $5-$10 USD, otherwise I wouldn't have bothered leaving this review. I'll still be playing, but I'm a masochist, or a sadist. It's hard to say.

[h1] MORDHAU is a multiplayer medieval game, where the player gets a chance to create his own type of a knight, customize it any way he likes and jump straight forward into the bloody battle. The game is strongly focused on skill-based sword fights and the player’s ability to work as a team. [/h1] 

[b] Pros: [/b]

+ Massive 64 players battles
+ Pleasant graphics
+ Huge variety of different weapons and armors that lets the player pick a perfect playstyle that will fit his needs
+ In-depth character customization
+ Bloody and gore battles, full of realistic limbs/heads chopping off
+ Extremely realistic battles 

[b] Cons: [/b]

- Lack of maps, by the moment of writing the review the game has only four maps
- Some balance issues
- Every time the player fights against the red team, their blue teammates may be covered in blood which can lead to unintentional teamkill and overall confusion
- The developers didn't spend much time working on the party system when playing with friends
- Pretty toxic community

MORDHAU was a game that really surprised me, simply because I was not hyped about it and I never even knew about its existence. On top of that, I was really disappointed by the game's predecessors and I was kinda skeptical about Mordhau as well. 

However, the game became extremely popular when it was released and after seeing multiple different articles all over the internet, I decided to grab it and give it a chance. 

To be honest, it was one of the best experiences I had this year so far and this game really made my weekend. This game was able to significantly fix all the problems and mistakes that have been made by its predecessors and this is probably the best part about this game. MORDHAU still has lots of issues and problems and has to be polished, but it can already bring you hundreds of hours of pure fun. But first things first.

[h1] Story [/h1]

Instead of wasting their time and budget on making a story, the developers decided to focus on multiplayer aspects of the game. That means that right now, MORDHAU doesn't have any story campaign in its current state and it comes with three different multiplayer modes instead.

[h1] Gameplay [/h1]

MORDHAU is a skill-based slasher medieval action game, where the player really has to learn how to fight properly. Otherwise, the whole game will turn into brainless sword/polearm/axe swinging, where players chase for having as much kills as possible. The whole idea of the fights is to block properly, make counter attacks with perfect timing or even knock your enemies with your feet. It sounds pretty easy at the beginning, but once you start playing and getting into the game, you can really feel that this game is a perfect definition of “easy to learn, hard to master”. 

The best part about MORDHAU is that it doesn’t force you to dive into the battle swinging with your sword or big polearm. The player always has an option to play as an archer, staying somewhere in the back, covering his teammates and defending the castle, which is also really important. Or they can even take care of ballista and shoot enemies from the distance doing an enormous amount of damage to the enemies’ horde. 

And this is something what I really love about MORDHAU: you start to play it, you try out every single class, save some gold, level up and then you find out that the game lets you create your own character, which you can fully customize just the way you like it. This is where the game starts to shine and where it really becomes absolutely fun and insane at the same time. 

On the customization screen, you will see sixteen points available to spend to create the dream knight. You can spend these points to pick some useful perks, buy armor and weapons. The trick is that you have to find a perfect balance between the points you spend for weapon, armor, and perks that will fit your playstyle. For example, you can spend most of the points for the heavy armor and take a bit weaker weapon, or you can go absolutely naked but pick the most expensive weapon and a bunch of perks. Seriously, the variety is huge and you can be as creative as you wish. 

The game offers you three different modes and it’s really important to state that I was only amused by the Frontline. I have a strong feeling that the whole game has been developed for this mode first of all and other modes are just a pleasant bonus where you can have some fun when you are tired of Frontline. Frontline is a typical Deathmatch-alike mode, where 64 players played in two teams, equally separated with an ultimate goal to control points and complete different tasks during the game. The first team that reaches 1000 points win, easy as that. There is also a Battle Royale mode, well I guess I don’t have to explain what this mode is about. And AI Horde mode, where the players have to defend the base from a horde of enemies. 

When you play Frontline, the biggest problem you face is playing on a blue team. The trick is that guys from the blue team will be covered in the blood eventually that can lead to unintentional teamkill and overall confusion. It can be really hard to differentiate during the intense battles where is the real red color and where are your teammates covered in blood.  

MORDHAU is not perfect in its current state and you can’t ignore it. It has only a few maps, but the good news that developers announced that they are working on the new maps already. This game also has some balance issues where some of the weapons feel much more powerful than others. And of course, such kind of a problem leads to the toxic community, where players yell in the game chat tons of offensive stuff blaming everyone.

I was pretty sad when I wanted to play with my friend in a group and it turned out to be a complete disaster. It feels like this option is still in development or something, but it’s definitely unpolished and not finished at all. By the moment we logged into a game, we never saw each other on the map or some kind of group shown on the screen identifying that we were playing together. We were even able to play for the different teams and it was absolutely confusing, really looking forward to seeing this issue fixed soon.      

[h1] Graphics [/h1]

Graphics is not outstanding in MORDHAU, it looks a bit outdated and doesn’t make your jaw drop on the floor. It shouldn’t be a big problem for you, simply because you will be focused on the battles all the time. Besides, the whole game has been funded by Kickstarter backers an developed by a small company, so the result is already not that bad. 

[h1] Sound [/h1]

Sound is absolutely gorgeous in this game: you will hear epic music during the battles, motivational screams of the players, which can be triggered by pressing a specific button and realistic sounds of running horses, launching ballistic and crossing swords.

[h1] Conclusion [/h1]

I absolutely love MORDHAU. This game can be super fun and relaxing and challenging at the same time. It offers you tons of options in customizing and creating your character. I really wish that the developers will fix all the problems it has now and will continue to update it.

MORDHAU is a 1st/3rd person medieval fighter game by Triternion and a spiritual successor to Chivalry, a game by Torn Banner Studios from years ago. It's essentially a shooter, but with swords and bows instead of guns. You play from a handful of premade classes (or make your own) and duke it out with and against other players on about a dozen maps in a variety of modes, ranging from simple Team Deathmatch to large scale battles complete with horses and siege weapons in Invasion and Frontlines.

If any of this sounds fun to you, it's because it is. Mordhau is an absolute blast when you first get to experience it. The meat of the game isn't just random sword swings- you have special mechanics like attacking at the same time to make you and your opponent's weapons graze off eachother, kicks to disrupt enemies that are too close, the dreaded feint, and a few others. Mordhau's combat is easily its strongest point, and you can tell a ton of love went into it specifically. It's an easy thing to learn all of your different options in combat, but using them properly is another story. On the surface it makes for an easy to use, hard to master combat system that should reward you for knowing the mechanics and taking the time to learn and apply them.

Beyond the combat is customization- it's robust to say the least. You can customize anything from your character's face to their voice, and there are dozens of different armors of varying strength to suit whatever playstyle you want. Do you want to be a heavily armored knight running around with a longsword? Maybe a low armor but fast moving soldier with something heavier like a zweihander? Maybe just a naked dude smacking people with a giant stick? You can do any of that and more. The class creator lets you throw together pretty much anything on a point limit, where every item you add reduces the available points by X amount. It's fun to mix and match and create alternate playstyles, and I have 30 or so classes that I love to switch between.

I love Mordhau. But I don't recommend it to anyone who hasn't bought it or isn't willing to put in many hours, for a small number of reasons that stack up and turn a product of love into something that's nothing like what I expected when I saw the gameplay of it two years ago.

Remember that combat system? It has a lot of mechanics which should make for something deep and rewarding. However, high level play ends up just revolving around two specific mechanics- drags and accels. Dragging is slowing your swing down mid-swing, and accel is the opposite, making it hit faster. These mechanics need to exist in the game so that everything isn't always 100% readable. The issue is, it makes gameplay turn into a guessing game rather than a fight of who plays better. Drags and accels are generally 100% safe in the sense that ALL other mechanics- kicks, feints, chambers (matching attack type and direction to punish aggressive opponents) and more all have setbacks, like consuming stamina or in the case of kicks, leaving you wide open to a counter attack if you miss. Drags & accels have none of this, and it's possible to slow your swing down to the point of near-stopping while you still get lovetapped for over half your HP bar, or swinging so blindingly fast that you have an extremely small window to react. [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jPQ81Zh-yEg] Here's what I mean. [/url] This isn't mine and I am not using it to call negative attention to the maker or anything, it's just the most immediate example since I have no recording software. This is a far cry from the [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=THKTfTFVfOY] Gameplay trailer [/url] from two years ago that showcased the intense combat that hyped me for it so much after Chivalry's ballerina antics.

Now that the game has been out for some months, people have learned how to use these mechanics to their 'fullest'. In my experience this means duels devolving into a fight of who can throw their mouse around the most, or who can obfuscate their attacks the best. It's nowhere near Chivlary's level of ridiculousness, but it's far from the combat trailers that sold me on it and made me say "Yes, give me this game right now!"

Map design is questionable at best, as many TDM maps allow sides to nearly get into eachothers' spawns, or are so tunneled in that it's easy to spawncamp. 32v32 modes (Invasion and Frontlines) have a handful of maps that still cause rolls for one side. I feel like this is partially alleviated by the release of Invasion, but Frontlines still suffers hard on some maps. (Looking at you, Camp.) 

I also feel that there is a weapon and perk imbalance in that a handful of weapons are overtuned for their cost to what they provide ratio. Things like the Eveningstar reign supreme much of the time, and the War Axe's short 'active' attack window coupled with the fact that it can two-shot you almost guaranteed even with heavy armor makes these weapons and a few others extremely common. The Messer also has notoriously janky one-handed swing animations that make it a chore to deal with. The meta is so set in stone that while you can play around it for sure, for me it has sucked a lot of the fun out as most people use the same small pool of weapons and the same one or two perks, like Bloodlust which for 5 class creation points (you get 16 [now 48] I believe) lets you regen to 100 HP on a kill. It makes fighting the same thing for the umpteenth time get stale. The devs also recently nerfed shields into the ground so there's even less variety now.

The community is also hit or miss. You'll find anything from meme-spouting fun havers to people making racist remarks just to be edgy, to the veterans telling you to just "Get good". There's a chat filter if you're soft and in need of blocking out what people say, but obviously it's a little hard to block out something that directly impacts gameplay like people that troll matches by building emplacements so you're stuck as soon as you spawn, or just clog up doorways to set your team back til you kick them. You can find less abrasive people from time to time, but in my experience I see a lot of the former.

Speaking of the devs- development time for updates is notoriously slow due to Triternion being a small dev team. I wouldn't have an issue with this, but with how poor of a state the game is in, slow development time does nothing to ease core issues like weapon imbalance and poor map design. There's been a total of around 3 major updates that have included one new map (which recently got a rework since it was widely regarded as unfun), a couple of new weapons, a ranked duel mode, new cosmetics and a system that seemed to try to make combat faster paced by shortening how long your 'active' attack window was (I think this was to combat dragging being super meta, but in turn made accels lightning fast) which got veto'd and rolled back just a couple days later.

Mordhau is way more of a medieval fighter than Chivalry could ever hope to be, even with its flaws. I'll likely continue to play it from time to time, even though it does frustrate me often and I generally play no more than a couple matches before remembering why I quit last time- nothing changes. The meta is stale and revolves around the same pool of weapons and couple of combat mechanics. New content is sparse and so far hasn't been super meaningful. 

Again, I love Mordhau. But Steam asks if I recommend it. In its current state Mordhau feels like a game that favors spazzy combat tactics instead of intense swordfights, with a slow changing game state that doesn't deviate from the meta. Once the honeymoon wears off, you might think like me. To a new player- unless you're willing to deal with a harsh learning curve of veterans that have many hours, can put up with the lack of content and are okay with an unchanging meta, stay far away and wait for the game to improve. If it ever does. I hope it does.

Mordhau is an odd rarity of a game which has had many troublesome design choices that have ultimately led to its slow loss of players. As a newcomer to Mordhau, the experience -- while still including some occasionally fun moments I could not have captured from any other game -- is a very slow and agonising series of defeats with no clear sign of improvement or progression in skill, being constantly dominated by the typical sweaty Ploomer or the Maulester who exploits the already broken mechanics of the game and quite frankly makes the game more cancerous than it should be. 

The developers have clearly lost faith and interest in the game, considering the lack of updates (or patches in this case) with a similar approach to TF2, simply adding cosmetics and random bug-fixes for practically useless things nobody really needed to be 'fixed' in the first place. The developers, also having completely forgotten the purpose of Mordhau's die-hard community of talented, and entirely proficient mod developers who had shown an interest in providing any sort of game-mode to help Mordhau grow again.

Mordhau has an extremely toxic and sweaty playerbase, which is slowly leeching off of the casual player-base until their inevitable extinction. The odds of finding any casual player anymore is starting to grow slim, and the fact than an entire region of players is practically gone (OCE), is just saddening, although I do not play in that region.

It was clear to me that a few warning signs popped up in my head when I first played this game, especially since the developers hadn't properly established their target audience -- competitive or casual -- so they simply blended these two vastly different groups together hastily in an attempt to steal the initial following of players and melee slashers at the time.

Despite being developed by some ex-Chivalry players, I was surprised to see that the game had one-of-a-kind netcode that was far more superior than any other triple A game I'd ever seen, and the combat felt quite satisfying. However, after many patches, with many issues arising during this time, there is still an insane amount of exploiting that exists in the game, and it seems like every patch keeps missing the mark and entire flaw and bug of each patch and instead focusing on something incredibly pointless instead to further ruin the game.

Mordhau was - and in many ways still is - one of the finest multiplayer games I’ve ever played. Its melee combat system remains one of the most intricate and satisfying mechanics in gaming. It took what Chivalry built, refined it, and surpassed it in (almost) every conceivable way. When it launched, it felt 
[i]alive[/i].

The movement was fluid, the combat was sharp and responsive. Every swing, every parry, every feint carried weight. The maps were... alright..., and even the bots held their own reasonably well. Nothing meaningful was locked behind a grind or a paywall, only cosmetics, and even those felt fair for the most part. Servers developed their own small communities, each with its own culture and regulars. You’d recognize names, rivals, even friends. It was, for a time, something truly special.

But despite all of that, I can’t recommend Mordhau anymore. And there’s only one reason why:

[b]If you’re a new player, you’re going to hate it. [/b] 

Updates came few and far between, each one smaller and more disappointing than the last. Promises faded into silence, and the developers’ once-bright enthusiasm dimmed into neglect. The community began to crumble. And with no fresh content, no new players, and no reason to stay, people left.

Almost everyone who once populated the game has moved on, and what remains is a core of hardened veterans: players who have spent thousands of hours mastering every feint, chamber, riposte, and emote abuse. They know every weapon’s swing radius, mastered every animation trick, and got their timings precise to the millisecond. If you’re just starting out, you will be torn apart before you can even raise your sword.

There’s no learning curve. It's a learning mountain climb. You’ll have to endure hundreds of hours of brutal, demoralizing losses before you start to stand a chance.

It’s tragic, because Mordhau is not a bad game, in fact, it’s one of my all-time favorites. But without fresh blood, it’s a corpse animated by the ghosts of those who refused to move on.

For once, it’s fair to use the phrase:
This is a dead game.

Rest in peace, Mordhau.
You were brilliant, and you deserved better.

Let me begin with this: This game could soon die. I'm not sure if it will, I'd bet that some players will be left in it, but Chivalry 2 is a game with attachments to a previous title that people hold much dearer to their hearts. 

However, having played chivalry, I can say that I thoroughly enjoy Mordhau over chivalry. 

Concerning humor, many people will attempt to say that Mordhau is full of toxic/sweaty/competitive players who can't get over themselves. This is simply false. I have easily spent 50% of my duels emoting for 20 minutes and having a whale of a time before we finally conceded to the booing audience and fought. Going into any horde or frontline server, most people are pretty friendly or just there to mess around and have fun. Even ranked matches generally have pretty friendly people, provided you're friendly to them first. It's not uncommon to find players just playing a lute while troops from both sides dance to the "music" (comprised entirely of the  four notes you can play on a lute). As long as you're not dealing with an asshole or someone who takes the game too seriously, making the other players laugh blurs the line between friend and foe for a time.

Some people have a problem with the fact that bows feel useless, let me just lay that issue to rest by saying that in Mordhau bows are pretty realistic. It's not a gun, this is not a first person shooter, and a metal helmet will mostly protect from an arrow. The human body is pretty durable so if an arrow doesn't hit your mostly unguarded head, you'll probably survive. If you want a gun, become a server admin and type "ParryThis" in the console. You'll get a 1411. Wins every duel.

I encounter toxic players every so often, if you hop on to a duel server one will show up eventually. Trolls and sweaty players, for the most part. The sort that types "your not worth my time" and "ez" in the chat post-fight. They're not especially common, vote-kicking them (which you're free to do at any time no matter your status in the server) pretty much gives them the final word of "mad cuz bad" before they leave the server for the night. If you have two people on a mostly inactive duel server and one shows up, votekick once they break the server rules and you'll not come out of the game any worse for it. 

The melee combat is pretty in-depth, and while it's a little too readable to be realistic the game makes up for that with a system that greatly rewards personal skill. If you head into a duel server, expect to die at first, but also expect that if you ask someone to give you some pointers, they will. Armed with those pointers, you'll find yourself building the reflexes and doing better over time. This is greatly aided by the fact that there are countless weapons, each of them different in swing times and damage to certain parts with certain armor. The weight of the armor you wear, though not the level you unlock it at, also matters, and in general the gear capacity system helps to let people find their unique fighting style. 

This must quickly be said of the fighting, the model of the weapon and the model of you is what matters (provided no lag shenanigans). If you get hit by the arc of the weapon, meaning the weapon's model hits you as it is being swung, you take damage. If you block as it does that, you don't take damage but you do lose stamina. If your weapon hits their shield, they don't take damage. As a result, you'll see players "dragging", meaning they intentionally lengthen the swing of their weapon, to throw off your parry. You'll see them accelerating, meaning the opposite of dragging, to get you with the beginning of their swing and potentially catch you off guard. nothing is unparryable, I've parried it all. Making your opponent parry early or late is the key to hitting them, though. Unless they run out of stamina first, then it's just open sesame before they can pick their weapon back up. 

Speaking of the weight of the armor you wear as opposed to the level you unlock it at, some weapons and armor need to be purchased with Gold, which you earn through playing the game. Some armor also requires that you be a certain level to purchase it. This is all EXCLUSIVELY COSMETIC. You get to look cooler as you level up, but there is no difference in stats between the basic helmet and the imposing Greathelm. They're both heavy armor, and that's as far as it goes. Weapons are, for the most part, all viable if you can make them work with your playstyle, and you get access to a slightly higher variety of them as you level up. My advice is go and look for weapons in Horde Mode, try them out, and if you like them you can purchase them for non-horde gameplay. 

It cannot be stressed enough that this game has z e r o microtransactions. You buy it, you might buy the supporter bundle, and that's all you can purchase. Otherwise, Gold is earned after each match and it's not hard to get pretty mass quantities of it. Horde mode is best for farming it, giving you 1500-3000 for getting pretty late into the waves if you successfully participated in the rounds by killing a few before The Little Red Men threw 4,000 firebombs your direction (beware wave 18). To put that in perspective, the most expensive skins in the game cost about 50,000. Most skins for weapons and armor cost between 500 and 4000. you'll get around 100 for a ranked duel match and typically around 500 for a session of a duel server, which is an FFA game mode with rules in place to let players just run around and duel. Most cosmetics are unlocked before level 25, and XP is pretty much farmed through the same methods. If you really don't want to play the game in order to get your cosmetics, there's even a couple AFK servers out there which provide you with an AutoHotKey script to avoid being AFK disconnected, so there's just a horde of AFK people in the back of the map while a few willing souls get to be overpowered and do wave after wave of horde mode. Gives around 10,000 if you leave it on overnight, since technically you don't get any bonuses for killing anybody so it's slower than playing horde mode for 8 hours straight, but at the same time I wouldn't blame you for just not wanting to do that. I don't like horde mode much, meself, and you'll find me lurking around AFK servers for a couple hours at a time if I see a cosmetic and thiink to myself "Must acquire". 

Overall, Mordhau is a game that lets you do what you want in a medieval fighting situation, even if what you want is messing around with emotes and a lute. You can fight with pitchforks and frying pans if you really want to, or you can take it a bit more seriously and learn your favorite weapon. No matter what, if you enjoy the game, you'll find a community in a server that's right for you. You'll find your niche, and when you do the game will become a source for memories, memes, and good times. 

If you dispute what I say here, Pay your respects to the don and tell me why.

MORDHAU is a genuinely good game… and that’s what makes this sting.
The melee combat is still some of the best in the genre: weighty, skill-based, and ridiculously satisfying when it clicks. When matches are lively, it can feel like medieval chaos in the best way.

But it also feels abandoned. Updates have slowed to a crawl, and the community has thinned out, which makes the game feel like it’s fading. On top of that, the core loop starts to get stale after a while. Once you’ve done the same modes and fights enough times, it turns into “queue, swing, respawn, repeat” with less and less to chase.

If you’re new and can catch it on sale, there’s absolutely fun to be had, especially if you enjoy high-skill melee games. Just don’t expect a living, growing game anymore.

Verdict: Great combat, great moments, but a shrinking playerbase and a stale loop hold it back.

Level 57, been playing this game since its release and while it was certainly intended to be an ambitious project, it failed and continues to fail so miserably.

I will start with good sides before I'll move on to its tragic flaws which unfortunately, are why after so many played hours, I'm still giving it a negative review. 

First of all, the combat is a massive improvement from Chivalry. It's similar but so much better. In addition to feints, you get morphs, chambers, alternative grips, items that can be build like barricades or spikes, accesories and even mobile ballistas. You can dodge swings by kneeling, you can pick up weapons and throw them. (You can even pull an axe from your buddies face and throw it at the opponent).  There are drags and accels but nowhere as ridiculous as in Chivalry.

And of course, there are horses. A lot of players complain about them but truth be told, until the invention of tank, cavalry owned most of battlefields and so it does in this game.

You can also create your own warrior, face and all (Although Oblivion had better faces), select weapons and armor for him as well as perks. 

And this is where the fun ends.

Due to its extremaly steep learning curve (tutorial will teach you only the most basic things), the game is unforgiving for new players. If you play Frontline (which is where the game shines), you'll get obliterated and if you decide to duel on Free for All servers (There are no duel servers), you'll get wtfpwned by dudes who are masters at overhead drags. Matchmaking doesn't exist. There are no ranked servers. Newbs and veterans all end up together playing the same match.

The best way to learn ANYTHING is to either accept the fact you're going to die hundreds of times for the first month of playing, watch YT videos or team up with someone who'll teach you. 

But why bother anyway?

The server stability leaves a lot to be desired. You need to seek a server closest to where you live for the best stability so forget about playing with your buddy who lives further away. Freezing and lag spikes make it unplayable. I've been playing sh!tload of online games and never had these issues but according to Devs, "It's our firewall settings" (I'll roast the all-knowing Devs later).

Ping should be an absolute priority in a game based on a melee combat!

Moreover, the community in this game...my goodness. It's like 4.chan's /pol channel simulator. The chat is usually a place for the debates about the lost glory of Aryan race or ethnic origin of various players and occasional "fight me irl" bickering by teenage keyboard knights.

Griefers and trolls everywhere, guys barricading their own team inside spawn points, setting up spikes and bear traps to prank their own team. Try to stop them and they will have you votekicked for teamkilling. Speaking of which, the votekick is a broken, abused feature. Anyone can do it for whatever reason and as soon as others see someone being votekicked, they usually vote yes. 

The maps are few and they are imbalanced as hell. On Frontline, you can tell which team is going to win by which map is being played. There are only TWO balanced maps (Grad and Camp), otherwise, its either one team spawning too close to the middle point (control of which decides about the main ticket advantage) or another team having far more difficult objectives to accomplish. The maps are poorly designed, favouring only one team and the Devs "fix" them only by switching advantage to the other team.

The Devs, oh yes....where are they? They released the game, earned a lot of money and apparently, went to spend it all in Tahiti or Hawaii.  Hey, it's summer right? 

Well, no if you've got a lot of issues to fix and you should be doing it instead of chilling. The playerbase is dropping fast. It's been TWO months since the last patch. Oh, and that patch...they gave us a new map called Crossroads! Great news, right?

Not really. Crossroads is one of the worse, inbalanced maps I've seen in my gaming experience. Then of course, they "fixed" it by completely ruining another's team spawn point. 

The imbalance of maps causes players to switch from one team to another because they simply know which one is going to win.

You might have read on other gaming portals about Devs yapping about introducing playable female characters. 

Well, it appears that getting woke is more important than fixing game issues that have been present here since day one: This game needs better servers, more community regulations, complete map overhaul, a new content but has ZERO support.

Give this game a wide berth. Wait for a year until it either dies out (my prediction) or gets better (With the Devs attitude however? Naaaah).

Don't give Triterion your money. They don't deserve it and it will most likely finance their holidays which they should be spending by fixing this steaming pile of dung.

If you enjoyed Chivalry: Medieval Warfare and have been waiting for a sequel not involving hero shooter mechanics and magic spells, this is the game for you. Skill-based combat meets chaotic battlefields littered with the bodies of the fallen (or what's left of them, anyways). 
An in-depth character customization system lets you create your own virtual avatar or mix and match weapons and armor for the perfect loadout, and a progression mechanic keeps you engaged with the game if that's your thing. 
Looking for Battle Royale? There is an official BR mode waiting for you in the matchmaking queue. Battlefield-style large scale engagements? Frontlines is there for you, with capture points, objectives, horses and other niceties. Not big on PvP? Horde mode would like to have a word, if you please (the AI isn't super smart, but it can hold its own in a fight).
Old school deathmatch/TDM? It's there too. Community servers? You betcha.

Bugs and some server stability issues? Yeah, we got those too, but for a game created by a team of just eleven people working from all corners of the globe, Mordhau is an amazing achievement.

I'd like to start this off by saying that Mordhau is a very well made game, but there's quite a few reasons that I would personally not recommend buying this game unless you are within the handful of people that have what it takes to enjoy a game like this.

If you describe yourself as a very competitive player, and you strive to top the leaderboards of every game, then be prepared to spend 500+ if not more hours learning the ins and outs of combat in this game to even come close to the top of the leaderboard. The skill ceiling is very high in this game, and a majority of the playerbase nowadays are seasoned vets who've clocked hundreds if not thousands of hours into the game making them practically unstoppable. I love games with high skill ceilings such as Rocket League, but the problem that Mordhau has with it's skill ceiling is that newer players will get stomped every time. This leads me to my next point.

Mordhau makes me experience emotions that I rarely ever get to experience from other video games. I can't think of another video game that is able to recreate the feeling of winning a 3v1 situation where everyone is actively trying to kill you. At the same time, I have also never felt as helpless and out of options in a video game as when going up against a tryhard in Mordhau. Swinging and delaying attacks, feinting, chambering and morphing your attacks against one really sweaty player who blocks all of it, and then kills you with one swing is a feeling that just sucks. Both of those things will happen in every game, but chances are you will just end up remembering that one guy on the other team who killed you 6 times without you even landing a hit on them. It ends up feeling like you're trying to fight a brick wall, and the feeling can snowball and end up ruining a game for you.

One last thing to note about tryhards is that they fill up a good chunk of every game. You will notice yourself dying to the same handful of people in every game.

At the end of the day, I'd only really recommend this game for two types of players. 
1) Those who do not take the game seriously and troll / mess around in every game
or 
2) The ultra competitive, who get their enjoyment of a game out of seeing improvement, who can keep a level head, and manage their emotions well.

Since I feel that this game can only fit well for those two types of players, I just can't recommend a purchase of the game to anyone who doesn't fit under those two descriptions. It's probably worth a pickup if it goes on sale though

[h3] Goodbye Mordhau [/h3]
Witnessing the steady decline of Mordhau's playerbase has left me sad and hopeless for this game's future.
Mordhau once had a peak player count of just over 60,000 players; that was over 6 years ago now and it's been declining ever since.
Recently, it's average player count has officially dropped below 1,000 concurrent players and continues to drop with every passing month.
As I type this review, there are currently only 360 players online.

I'm not sure if there's any hope of revival for Mordhau anymore.
There are a few clans and communities dedicated to trying to keep the game alive, but they're practically the entire playerbase now and even their active members are dwindling. Plus, the majority of active players are skilled veterans and very competitive, making it extremely hard for new players to actually get into the game, let alone to stay long enough to hold their own. And not to mention how in many regions, new players can't even play due to the lack of servers.

And, above all, the devs themselves have abandoned the game.
It's last released content and patch were nearly a year ago, and before that, almost two years since the last new map. I don't even think the moderation team is active anymore, but I'm sure some would argue they never were. There wasn't/isn't even an anti-cheat.

I'm sorry, but as of September 2025, [b] Mordhau is Dead. [/b]
